summary: Mudagamuwe Maithrimurthi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD from the University of Hamburg in 1999 under Lambert Schmithausen, and held posts at Leipzig University (attested 2005) and Heidelberg University (attested 2007–2009).

Muhammad Ashraf Khan is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He has served as Deputy Director at the Taxila Museum, Director at the Department of Archaeology and Museums of Andhra Pradesh, and Director at Quaid-i-Azam University (attested 2019).
Mumon Yamada (1900–1988) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Hanazono University, where he later served as president from circa 1949 to 1978.

Mun-keat Choong specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Paramadhamma Buddhist Institute (1982) and Komazawa University (BA ~1986–1990), followed by the University of Queensland, where he earned an MA under Roderick S. Bucknell (~1992–1994) and a PhD (~1995–1998).

Munenobu Sakurai (b. 1961) works in Indology and Buddhist studies. After finishing his doctoral coursework at Tohoku University (~1986–1991), he served as assistant professor at Iwate University (~1995–2004) and became a professor at Tohoku University circa 2004.

Muneo Tokunaga (1945–2016) was an Indologist who completed graduate studies at Kyoto University (~1969–1971) and earned a PhD from Harvard University (~1974–1984). He held posts at Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1981–1989) and Kyoto University (~1989–2009, as professor from ~1990).
Mungunchimeg Batmunkh specializes in religious studies and Tibetology. She earned her Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna (attested 2010) under the supervision of Brigitte Marschall.

Murray Barnson Emeneau (1904–2005) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Dalhousie University, Balliol College, and Yale University, where he earned his PhD (1926–1931) under Franklin Edgerton. He became a professor at the University of California, Berkeley, in 1940.

Musashi Tachikawa (b. 1942), an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, earned doctorates from Harvard (under Daniel H. H. Ingalls) and Nagoya University. He held posts at Nagoya University, the National Museum of Ethnology, SOKENDAI, and Aichi Gakuin University.

Muzaffar Alam (b. 1947) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Jamia Millia Islamia, Aligarh Muslim University, and Jawaharlal Nehru University. He held posts at JNU (~1973–2001) and the University of Chicago (~2001), among other institutions.

Myles Dillon (1900–1972) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at University College Dublin (~1919–1922). He held academic posts at Trinity College Dublin, University College Dublin, the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and the Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies (~1949–1972).
Myoshin Fujitake (b. 1956) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He has served as a committee member for the Otani Society (attested 2000) and as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Otani University.
Mysore Hiriyanna (1871–1950) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Maharaja's College, Mysore (~1912–1927) and at the University of Mysore (~1916–1927).
Myōsei Tatsuguchi is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor (attested 1987) and later emeritus professor (attested 2015) at Ryukoku University.

Mónika Kiss is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. She pursued doctoral studies in Japanese Studies at Eötvös Loránd University under advisor Masanori Yamaji, also studying under Robert F. Rhodes and Nozomu Saito.
N. Aiyaswami Sastri was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a professor at Sri Venkateswara Oriental College (attested 1940) and Visva-Bharati University (attested 1971).

N. Veezhinathan is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who earned a PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University (1964) under A. Sankaran. He worked at Deccan College (1960–1963) and became Lecturer in Sanskrit at the University of Madras in 1964.

N. Venkataramanayya (1891–1976) was an Indologist and historian who studied under Ferrand Edward Corley. He served as Reader of Indian History and Archæology at the University of Madras and Deputy Director for Epigraphy for the Government of Andhra Pradesh.
Nagin J. Shah (b. 1931) is an Indologist and philosopher. He served as Acting Director of the L.D. Institute of Indology (attested 1968), where he succeeded Dalsukh D. Malvania.

Nalinaksha Dutt (1894–1973) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Chittagong College, the University of Calcutta (PhD ~1919–1921), and the University of London (DLitt ~1923–1925). He headed the Department of Pali at Calcutta (~1958–1960).
